subject: Data residency & retention: configurable retention + EU-only storage

Subject: Data residency & configurable retention options for FinCorp EU

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing our vendor short-list and have two compliance asks that are currently blockers for our Security & Legal teams:

- Ability to pin customer data to an EU-only storage region (no replication outside EU by default).
- Configurable retention windows per workspace (and per data type) with a programmatic deletion API and verifiable audit logs.

I've attached a spreadsheet that lists our minimum retention tiers, deletion SLAs, and examples of which artifact types need independent retention controls (embeddings, chat history, audit logs). Can you confirm whether Redwood currently supports any of this natively or if it would be a product/engineering project?

We'd like a rough timeline and an indication of whether this fits as a small surface change (weeks) or a multi-quarter project. Also — any known limitations (e.g., certain model types that can't run in EU regions) would be useful.

Can we schedule a 30-min call early next week to walk through the matrix?

Thanks,
Emma Richards
Head of Cloud Security
FinCorp EU

Quick answers up-front: Redwood does support regional model placement and can restrict runtime to EU regions for hosted deployments, but customer-configurable per-workspace retention and a formal deletion API with auditor-friendly proofs is not a fully productized capability today — it's a roadmap item with a few engineering caveats.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal triage (Marissa/Karthik): confirm critical acceptance criteria from the spreadsheet and call out high-risk items.
- Proposed kickoff call: Tue 2025-11-25 10:00 CET (if that works for you).
- In advance of the call, Marissa can share a short product-level checklist; Karthik will prepare a high-level technical approach (phases).

Attaching a short list of initial clarifying Qs here in case it helps prep the meeting:
1) Do you require zero-replication out of EU for backups, or is metadata-only replication acceptable?
2) Is per-tenant retention required, or do you need per-user/per-workspace/per-artifact granularity?
3) Do you need an immediate (synchronous) deletion API or eventual deletion with verifiable audit records?

Emma — would you be able to confirm availability for the Tue slot?

Thanks, Vivek. Emma — appreciate the spreadsheet. I've pulled out the product questions that affect scope and acceptance criteria below. These will help us scope a phased delivery we can propose on the call.

Product-level acceptance criteria (draft):
- EU-only data-at-rest: customer can select an EU storage residency flag for a dedicated workspace with no cross-region replication of content blobs (backups excluded — see question).
- Retention policy config: admin UI + API to set retention by artifact class (embeddings, generation logs, convo history), with default and max retention values and per-workspace override.
- Deletion API & audit: deletion request returns deletion token and job id; audit log entry created with timestamp, actor, scope. Option for a signed proof-of-deletion export (CSV) for auditors.
- Break-glass: emergency purge path for legal/DSARs with elevated controls and confirmation flow.

Open questions for Engineering:
- Does our storage layer support per-workspace isolation without tenant re-provisioning?
- Effort to add a signed proof-of-deletion export (what housing/crypto work is needed?).

Karthik — would you mind preparing a quick 2-slide tech summary for Tue's call outlining major risks, effort buckets (storage, API, audit logs, infra), and a preliminary ETA range (weeks vs quarters)?

Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data residency & configurable retention options for FinCorp EU

Hi all — quick technical readout before the call. I've kept this high-level so we can discuss trade-offs live.

Summary (high level):
- Regional storage (EU-only): possible for hosted customers by controlling where blobs and KV are provisioned. Caveat: models and some managed caches may have metadata or runtime traces in control plane services; we can mitigate by extending the private-control-plane option or updating our control-plane data minimization policy.

- Configurable retention: two implementation patterns: 1) policy layer + TTL on objects (fast to implement for new objects), 2) retroactive sweep and metadata migration for existing objects (more complex).

- Deletion API & proof: deletion job + write-once audit entry (hash + timestamp + signer) — we can build a 'signed deletion receipt' service; crypto and key management (KMS/HSM) integration will be required for auditor-signed proofs.

Phased delivery proposal (rough):
Phase 0 (3-4 weeks): scoping, infra spike, security review, and a minimal acceptance prototype for new workspaces (EU-only flag + basic TTL on new objects).
Phase 1 (2-3 months): retention config UI + retention-by-artifact API + backend TTL enforcement for new objects.
Phase 2 (2-4 months): deletion jobs for historical objects, signed proof-of-deletion, audit export, and integration with KMS.
Phase 3 (3-6 months): hardening, multi-tenant migration tooling (if customer wants to migrate existing data into EU-only), and compliance certification readiness (SOC2 evidence updates).

Risks / open items:
- Migration complexity for customers with large historical corpora (cost + downtime).
- Backup replication policy: our backup provider currently replicates encrypted chunks across regions for redundancy; contracting with them for EU-only backups will likely incur extra cost/SLAs.
- Model runtime artifacts: some models log usage telemetry to central control plane for billing/observability; we need to ensure those telemetry records are either (a) kept in EU, or (b) pseudonymized sufficiently.

I'll bring an estimate matrix to Tue's call. For the ask in the spreadsheet, a reasonable baseline to deliver the features for new workspaces is ~3 months from kickoff (Phase 0 + Phase 1), with full historical migration and signed proofs taking an additional 3-6 months depending on scope.

Attachment: implementation-scope-snapshot.pdf

-Karthik
Engineering Lead, Infra & Serving
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side before the call:

- Backups: EU-only backups are a hard requirement for our legal team. If your current backup partner can't guarantee EU-only replication, we'd need to see contract language or explore alternative approaches (e.g., bring-your-own-key and EU-only managed storage).
- Signed deletion receipts: must be verifiable by a 3rd-party auditor (we will ask for the verification flow during SOC2 assessment).
- Telemetry: pseudonymization is acceptable if we can map telemetry to customer records on request (audit link).

We'll bring two Security Engineers and a Legal lead to the Tue 11/25 call. Can you send a proposed agenda and the 2-slide tech summary beforehand?

Best,
Emma
